assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only silent-witch:monica-everett@light-novel#v1-character-monograph (the canonical V1 character monograph, version 1.0) at basis_commit, read in full as reviewed repository analysis of the Japanese light novels V01-V12 with the companions IV -after- (AFTER04) and IX -extra- (EXTRA09) and the two -another- prequel volumes, as closed at snapshot 60b21a7 (sixteen units). The prequels are used only as marked retrospection, and paratext is cited only as paratext. The monograph was written by a fresh-context analyst and checked mechanically and for knowledge boundaries by the integrator; neither reread the Japanese source, and owner semantic acceptance is not claimed. The master ledger, the readings and their observation registers, the specialist and relationship arguments, and the project's own reconstruction-readiness assessment are not curated evidence on this subject, and nothing is borrowed from them. No web serial, adaptation, translation or Codex G2 material is used, and the evaluator inspected no primary source.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: Evidence runs from Monica Everett's childhood with her father, Venedict Rain, through the end of V12. Her past (her father's execution when she was ten, about a year with her paternal uncle, Minerva, the Sage selection at fifteen, the hut and the Worgan black dragon) is her knowledge at every story state, though the reader learns it out of order (dream in V01, delirium in V02, memory in V03, the sober V04 prologue). Assessed states follow the monograph's fifteen located transitions: V01 baseline and speech acts; V02 duty adopted; V03 renunciation of Bernie Jones's approval and the hand held out; V04 split at the failure of numbers when Cyril Ashley is threatened (V04 obs. 090, 096-097); AFTER04; V05 split at the outward turn of the numbers and the vow for her father (V05 obs. 139-144, 170-180); V06 split at the anger named (V06 obs. 154-155); V07 from the first request for help (V07 obs. 005); V08 split at the decision for rescue over justice (V08 obs. 182) and the self-disclosure before the council (V08 obs. 283, 291); V09 council and coda; EXTRA09 frames; V10; V11 split at her study of a master's responsibility (V11 obs. 142, 192-194); and V12, with her feelings toward Cyril Ashley and Isaac Walker unnamed. Before V08 she knows Isaac Walker only as the prince Felix. No state after V12 is established.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, including the owner calibration rulings; evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The monograph gives a discriminating account of Monica Everett: silence and number are one survival mechanism that is re-tasked rather than removed (refuge in V01, weapon and then limit in V04, evidence in V05, a master's measure in V10); fear meeting a sentence someone else gave her is the mechanism of each change; her self-report lags her conduct, which lets it predict that she will understate and self-accuse ('makeweight', 'heartless', 'my ego'); and its coping structure says when the numbers fail (when people she knows are threatened, V04 obs. 090). It predicts her mistakes: losing a negotiation she came to unprepared (V05 obs. 130), mercy imposed without consent (V07 obs. 126, V10 obs. 135), a standard set without a master's responsibility (V11 obs. 142), and meeting a feeling with instruments (V12 obs. 070). A would overclaim: the general line that she changes by running sentences given by others is the monograph's own synthesis, no ledger claim states it in that form, and the rival reading that her development is situational keeps strong support. C would understate an account that says what changes her response and where it stops.

The monograph orders fifteen state transitions by unit with the mechanism the text shows for each (section 4.13), keeps diegetic, source and revelation order apart, and states what does not change: the stammer at V08 and V09, fear of tall men tied to her uncle at V12, crowds at V10. C would understate a located, causally explained developmental record. A is rejected: elapsed time between and within volumes is sparse, the prequels are retrospective, and the V12 state is left open by the text.

The monograph records written speech for Monica Everett: printed stammer marks (repeated syllables, internal ellipses, bitten final syllables) that persist at moments of courage; stable conditions of fluency (non-human listener; explaining a calculation, proof or ledger; anger at a botched formula; defending another person or correcting a fact; writing, where sentences are whole but event order is lost); polite forms to almost every human, plain forms to Nero throughout and to Lana Colette from V01's epilogue; habitual apology, replaced by thanks to Bartholomeus in V08; and located address (the honorific sama for Cyril Ashley, 'Treasurer Norton', Louis Miller as the only Sage called by given name, 'Monica' from V09). B would overclaim: the monograph quotes no Japanese, so no first-person form, sentence ending or lexicon is given, and there is no voice evidence. D would understate stable fluency conditions and address.

Section 7 locates recurring ordinary conduct with drivers: neglect of her body and food (V01 obs. 016, EXTRA09 obs. 019); measuring everything as her way of joining in (V01 obs. 049, EXTRA09 obs. 051, 105); keepsakes and the coffee pot; writing her name on nothing since Minerva; apology as habit. B would overclaim: much of this is comic set-pieces, and the monograph records that observation registers were consulted by targeted rows, so ordinary behaviour in AFTER04 and EXTRA09 may be under-represented, and some details are cited from synopses. D would understate patterns located across the series.

The monograph argues Monica Everett's side of each relationship by recipient with register, conduct and key change: Nero, Lana Colette, Cyril Ashley, Felix and then Isaac Walker, Louis Miller, Hilda Everett and Bernie Jones, with shorter entries for Isabelle Norton, Glen Dudley, Raul Roseburg, Ray Albright, Bartholomeus and Casey Grove. It states the conditioning rule: most fluent and bold with non-humans, in defence of others and when correcting a fact; weakest when a body is close or when she must speak for herself; changed most by those who give her a usable sentence. A is rejected: her V12 responses to Cyril Ashley and Isaac Walker are left unnamed, and the minor recipients are sampled in a few scenes.

Monica Everett has the most interior access in the series, and the monograph uses it to test self-report against conduct case by case (section 5), with the narration showing act and thought side by side. A would overclaim: the text leaves her V12 feelings unnamed, other characters' views of her are their beliefs, and the monograph did not reread the source.

Conflict conduct is located with conditions: her voice works when she defends another first (Bernie Jones, V03 obs. 042-045) or faces a broken formula (Thornley, V01 obs. 104-105); she accuses as a Sage when measurement gives her evidence (V05 obs. 139-142); she names anger and strikes (V06 obs. 154-155); she threatens an emperor and binds herself to a bargain (V08 obs. 061, 064); she bargains with Louis Miller on his terms, withholds from him and outmanoeuvres him; and she imposes silence on Clockford (V09 obs. 099). The countercases are recorded: numbers fail her when Cyril Ashley is threatened, and she loses an unprepared negotiation to Felix. A is rejected: physical pressure from Isaac Walker at V12 is met only with measurement, and new crisis responses beyond those sampled are open.

The monograph records located ethical priorities and tensions: she will not let another be falsely accused though she lets herself be (V01 obs. 059); she lies freely for others and to keep secrets; she refuses that anyone be sacrificed (V08 obs. 282); she chooses the living man over her father's name (V08 obs. 182, V09 obs. 120); she imposes mercy without consent and questions it herself (V10 obs. 135); and she builds the council's verdict on a staged truth the text presents as wise. B would overclaim: the text gives her the question of mercy without consent rather than an answer, does not judge her anger, and the discovery row claims no ethics dimension. D would understate located priorities that recur across V01, V08, V09 and V10.

The monograph treats the comedy as exact about her habits: genius and blind spot in one mind (the barrier that turns stairs into a slope, the prince's 'paw pads', prime numbers muttered to hide casting, a failed villainess, measuring a racing heart). It also records play, holding out her hand as a fellow ghost (V03 obs. 100). B would overclaim: she is mostly the object of the comedy rather than its agent, and her own sense of humour is not analyzed. D would understate a comic register located and explained as character.

One dedicated monograph covers all sixteen units, with 772 observation references and every ledger ID checked mechanically at integration, a name-and-reference check and stated defects. B would overclaim: neither the analyst nor the integrator reread the Japanese source, owner semantic acceptance is not claimed, observation registers were consulted by targeted rows, some details come from synopses, and SW-S unit assignment is positional. D would understate dedicated full-range coverage with located references.

Affirmative limits are recorded: the stammer persists through V09 (V08 obs. 009, V09 obs. 147); fear of tall men persists to V12 (V12 obs. 054); crowds remain hard and she cannot cast well on the move (V10 and V11 sections 7.1); she refuses help through V06 (V06 obs. 114-115, 130); she loses a negotiation she came to unprepared (V05 obs. 130); she first answers Rick in cold anger (V10 obs. 099); and she is blind to Isaac Walker's stated love (SW-R-0186). C would understate located countercases that bound the mechanisms.

Claims carry unit-prefixed observation numbers and ledger IDs; the three orders are kept apart; and knowledge is bookkept (Felix before V08, Isaac Walker after). A is rejected: within-volume ordering is coarse in places, elapsed story time is seldom given, and the prequels are retrospective.

conditions: Illustrative only, never quotation, and in a selected state: stammer marks when she speaks for herself or a body is close; fluent when explaining a calculation or proof, correcting a fact, defending another person or speaking to Nero.

Polite register to humans except Nero (plain throughout) and Lana Colette (plain from V01's epilogue); habitual apology before V08 and thanks thereafter where the evidence places them; address forms as recorded.
No Japanese first-person form, sentence ending or catchphrase is invented, since the evidence quotes none.
No line names her V12 feelings, gives her pre-V08 knowledge of Isaac Walker's identity, or is set after V12.
scenario_readiness.note: Stable fluency conditions, register and address constrain illustrative speech for Monica Everett. The absence of quoted forms keeps the use narrow.

conditions: Predictions are limited to the established mechanisms: retreat into numbers under fear; numbers that fail when someone she knows is threatened; a voice that works first in defence of another or against a broken formula; self-report that understates conduct; admission of a usable sentence from someone she trusts.
Whether she asks for help is set by the selected state: she refuses through V06 and asks from V07.
Her V12 feelings toward Cyril Ashley and Isaac Walker are presented as unnamed, never resolved.
Withheld identities stay withheld, and no open thread at V12 is resolved.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: One explicitly selected state among the monograph's transitions from V01 through V12 (for example V01-V02 as Monica Norton; V04 before or after numbers fail; V06 before the first request; V08 after the council reveal; V09 coda; V10-V12 as Isaac Walker's master). Prequel scenes are used only as retrospection, and no state after V12 is generated.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Recipients the monograph samples: Nero, Lana Colette, Cyril Ashley, Felix or Isaac Walker (under the V08 knowledge boundary), Louis Miller, Hilda Everett, Bernie Jones, or the minor recipients named in section 6 in their sampled roles. A stranger is sampled only as the lost stranger of V04 and audiences such as the Supreme Council; transfer to an unfamiliar adult is a separate, lower-confidence condition.
setting_constraints: The academy mission, Sage duties, magical combat, the hut and Southerndoor, and the master-apprentice household of the kinds shown.
No romance, physical intimacy or named feeling at V12.
No magic or politics beyond what the monograph attests.

scenario_readiness.note: The established mechanisms support bounded extrapolation for Monica Everett in sampled settings at a selected state. The text's refusal to name her V12 feelings excludes that domain.

conditions: Sampled settings only: baking or tea with friends, birthdays, homecomings with Hilda Everett, coffee with friends in Southerndoor, and household life with Nero and her apprentice.
Measuring is how she joins in; she neglects food, apologizes by habit, keeps keepsakes and fears touch and tall men as recorded.
Comic set-pieces are evidence of habit, not scripts; no invented private life outside the sampled scenes.
scenario_readiness.note: Located ordinary habits support narrow extrapolation for Monica Everett in the settings the monograph samples.

conditions: Only the located priorities: no one else falsely accused; no one sacrificed; the living person preferred to a name; lies for others and to keep secrets permitted.
Mercy imposed without consent is presented as a question she asks herself, never as a resolved principle.
No general moral philosophy is generated.
scenario_readiness.note: Located priorities support bounded deliberation for Monica Everett in situations like those sampled. The text leaves its central tension open.

The evidence affirmatively leaves Monica Everett's V12 shock, tears and shame concerning Cyril Ashley unnamed and records her blindness to Isaac Walker's stated love; Bridget's view is Bridget's belief. Generating romance would name what the text withholds.

conditions: Sampled functions only: chantless casting, with the spirit-king summoning as the one chant that names her; council treasurer work and reports; proofs and lectures at a board; Sage duties in public, where she writes rather than speaks; negotiation; mastering Isaac Walker, from a single standard to the three models of V11 and the corrected rule of V12.
Her limits are part of the model: unprepared negotiation, crowds, casting on the move.
No spell, institution or political act beyond what the monograph attests is generated.
scenario_readiness.note: Magic, Sage duties and mastership are densely sampled for Monica Everett, with located failures, supporting bounded extrapolation at a selected state.

known_limits.statement: The monograph was written by a fresh-context analyst from a snapshot of the ledgers and readings; neither the analyst nor the integrator reread the Japanese source, and owner semantic acceptance is not claimed.

The line that Monica Everett changes by running sentences given by others is the monograph's own synthesis, grounded in SW-C-0084 and the cited scenes; no single ledger claim states it in that general form.

The rival reading that her development is situational rather than dispositional keeps strong support: the stammer, fear of tall men and difficulty with crowds persist. The monograph's position is that what she attempts and whom she admits change while the reflexes of fear persist.
Monica Everett's V12 feelings toward Cyril Ashley and her response to Isaac Walker are left unnamed by the text and by the monograph (SW-C-0093, SW-P-0069).
The -another- volumes were read after V12 and are used only as marked retrospection; -another- upper supplies no narrative scene of her.
All speech evidence is printed prose described in English; the monograph quotes no Japanese, so no first-person form, sentence ending or lexicon is available, and there is no voice evidence.

Observation registers were consulted by targeted rows, some details are cited from reading synopses, and SW-S unit assignment is positional; ordinary behaviour in AFTER04 and EXTRA09 may be under-represented.

Identities the text withholds (the patron, the person Mary does not want to die, the seventh Sage, Hilda Everett's collaborator, the prison's attacker) stay withheld, and the ice spirit's identity with the pale-gold girl is implied only.
The ice spirit's plan, Isaac Walker's foretold loss, Mary's foreseen event and the seventh Sage's selection remain open at V12 and are not predicted.
No held-out validation, probe set or speech census is part of the curated evidence; generated dialogue is illustrative and its accuracy is untested.
